input.strategy_title: Make RHOAI more usable for enterprise teams
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Several strategic accounts have told field teams that RHOAI "feels hard to use
at enterprise scale". Feedback arrived through different channels and has not
been consolidated; the quotes below are representative but partially
contradictory. Leadership wants visible usability progress this release.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | — | Administration should be simpler. One account wants fewer configuration options exposed ("too many knobs"), another explicitly wants more fine-grained controls per project. |
| HLR-2 | — | Onboarding a new data scientist should take "less than a day". It is not defined what onboarding includes or where the day is currently spent. |
| HLR-3 | — | The platform should "integrate better" with existing enterprise tooling. No specific tools were named in the consolidated feedback. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Publish a whitepaper describing enterprise usability best practices on RHOAI. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks

## Out of Scope

Nothing has been explicitly scoped out.

## Open Questions

1. Which accounts' feedback takes precedence when requirements conflict (HLR-1)?
2. What does "onboarding" cover for HLR-2 — cluster access, project setup,
   first workbench, or first deployed model?
3. Which enterprise tools does HLR-3 actually mean?

# Simplify Dashboard administration defaults and option exposure

## Description

Executed if the enterprise-feedback precedence investigation selects the
simplification outcome (Branch A): the consolidated feedback favors reducing
the number of configuration options exposed to administrators ("too many
knobs"). This epic delivers a simpler administration experience in the
Dashboard by curating defaults and reducing exposed configuration options on
the administration surfaces named in the decision record.

## Scope

- Reduce the exposure of administration configuration options in the Dashboard
  administration surfaces to the curated set defined by the decision record,
  covering the configuration administered through the Dashboard's configuration
  CR (including the notebook culling settings administered there).
- Provide validated curated defaults for the options that are no longer
  exposed, so existing behavior is preserved without administrator action.
- Preserve an escape hatch for advanced administration needs consistent with
  the decision record, so power users are not cut off.
- Update related captions, labels, and references that fall out of these
  changes (no new documentation topics).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The count and set of exposed administration options matches the curated set
  in the decision record, validated against the Dashboard architecture
  context.
- Curated defaults preserve current platform behavior for existing
  installations; a regression suite demonstrates no behavioral change for
  untouched workflows.
- A rollback path or feature flag allows reverting to the previous option
  exposure, since this replaces an existing administration capability.
- The Dashboard build pipeline is green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1: Administration should be simpler — implements the "fewer knobs"
  direction selected when this branch executes.

## Gate

Selected by the outcome of the enterprise-feedback precedence investigation
(simplification direction). If that outcome does not hold, this epic is
removed and the fine-grained-controls branch executes instead; under a hybrid
outcome, both branches execute.

# Add fine-grained per-project administration controls

## Description

Executed if the enterprise-feedback precedence investigation selects the
fine-grained-controls outcome (Branch B): the consolidated feedback favors
more granular administration per project. This epic delivers per-project
administration controls in the Dashboard so administrators can tune settings
at project scope rather than only at platform scope.

## Scope

- Add per-project administration control surfaces in the Dashboard for the
  settings named in the decision record, covering configuration currently
  administered only at platform scope through the Dashboard's configuration
  CR (including per-workbench culling override capability where relevant).
- Define precedence behavior between platform-level defaults and per-project
  overrides per the decision record.
- Keep the platform-scope administration experience coherent with the new
  per-project controls (no duplicated or conflicting surfaces).
- Update related captions, labels, and references that fall out of these
  changes (no new documentation topics).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-project controls exist for the settings enumerated in the decision
  record, validated against the Dashboard architecture context.
- Platform defaults apply unchanged where no per-project override is set;
  a regression suite demonstrates no behavioral change for existing
  installations.
- A rollback path or feature flag allows disabling the per-project controls,
  since this replaces an existing administration capability.
- The Dashboard build pipeline is green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1: Administration should be simpler — implements the fine-grained
  per-project controls direction selected when this branch executes.

## Gate

Selected by the outcome of the enterprise-feedback precedence investigation
(fine-grained-controls direction). If that outcome does not hold, this epic is
removed and the simplification branch executes instead; under a hybrid
outcome, both branches execute.

# Resolve conflicting administration usability feedback

## Description

Enterprise feedback on administration complexity (HLR-1) is contradictory: one
strategic account wants fewer configuration options exposed ("too many knobs")
while another explicitly wants more fine-grained controls per project. This
Investigation consolidates the feedback arriving through the different
channels named in the problem statement, determines whose feedback takes
precedence (or whether a hybrid direction satisfies both), and produces a
decision record that selects the direction of the administration usability
work. The outcome determines which conditional implementation branch is
executed.

## Scope

- Consolidate all HLR-1 feedback from the channels described in the strategy
  and document the contradictions and their account sources.
- Determine the precedence rule (account tier, account count, feasibility, or
  a reconciling design) with input from field/account teams and product
  stakeholders.
- Enumerate the administration configuration surfaces affected, using the
  architecture context for the Dashboard (administration settings, including
  notebook culling defaults and overrides, are administered through the
  Dashboard's configuration CR).
- Produce a decision record naming the selected direction with one of the
  bounded outcomes:
  - **A — simplify**: reduce the number of exposed configuration options,
    curate defaults.
  - **B — fine-grained controls**: add per-project administration controls.
  - **Hybrid**: curated defaults plus a per-project advanced surface (both
    branches execute).

## Acceptance Criteria

- All HLR-1 feedback channels are consolidated and each contradiction is
  documented with its account source.
- A decision record exists that names the selected direction (A, B, or hybrid)
  with rationale and stakeholder sign-off from product/field ownership.
- The administration configuration surfaces in scope are enumerated and
  validated against the Dashboard architecture context.
- The decision record states the success criteria the selected direction will
  be measured against (e.g., count of exposed options, per-project override
  coverage).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1: Administration should be simpler; conflicting feedback on option
  exposure vs fine-grained controls. This investigation resolves the conflict
  that gates all HLR-1 implementation work.

# Define data-scientist onboarding scope and baseline

## Description

HLR-2 requires that onboarding a new data scientist takes "less than a day",
but the strategy does not define what onboarding includes or where the day is
currently spent. This Investigation defines the onboarding boundary (cluster
access, project setup, first workbench, or first deployed model), measures
where onboarding time is spent today, and produces a decision record that
scopes the onboarding implementation work and gives "less than a day" a
measurable definition.

Note on attribution: this investigation maps onboarding steps across both
affected components (Dashboard console flows and Notebooks workbench
lifecycle), so its scope is cross-component by nature. It is recorded under
the Notebooks component and Workbenches team as the primary owner of the
first-workbench onboarding leg; the decision record it produces apportions
each step to the owning component and team, and the console-side follow-up
work is carried by the Dashboard onboarding epic.

## Scope

- Evaluate the four candidate onboarding boundaries named in the strategy's
  open questions (cluster access, project setup, first workbench, first
  deployed model) and recommend which the target applies to.
- Map the current onboarding path end to end using the architecture context
  for Dashboard (project and workbench spawn flows) and Notebooks (workbench
  lifecycle, image selection, culling defaults administered through the
  Dashboard).
- Measure or estimate the time spent per step of the current path, identifying
  the steps that consume the "day" today (wait times, manual approvals,
  configuration, learning curve).
- Produce a decision record that: fixes the onboarding boundary, defines how
  "less than a day" is measured (from what start event to what first-success
  event), and lists which steps are in scope for improvement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision record fixes the onboarding boundary (which of the candidate
  scopes "onboarding" covers) with rationale and stakeholder sign-off.
- A baseline breakdown of current onboarding time per step exists, with the
  dominant time consumers identified.
- "Less than a day" has a measurable definition (start event, end event,
  measurement method) agreed in the decision record.
- The record identifies which improvement steps fall to the Dashboard
  onboarding experience and which to the workbench (Notebooks) experience, so
  each downstream workstream knows its scope.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2: Onboarding a new data scientist should take less than a day. This
  investigation resolves the undefined scope and baseline that gate all HLR-2
  implementation work.

# Identify enterprise tooling integration targets

## Description

HLR-3 asks that the platform "integrate better" with existing enterprise
tooling, but the consolidated feedback names no specific tools. This
Investigation identifies which enterprise tools the strategic accounts
actually mean, gathers the evidence from field/account teams, and assesses
feasibility and integration surface for each candidate on RHOAI, producing a
prioritized recommendation that scopes the integration implementation work.

## Scope

- Collect the underlying account feedback behind "integrate better" from
  field/account teams and name the specific enterprise tools referenced
  (e.g., identity providers, source control, ticketing, monitoring, data
  platforms — as identified, not assumed).
- For each named tool, assess the plausible integration surface on RHOAI
  (Dashboard console, authentication, CLI, APIs) using the architecture
  context, and note existing integration points (e.g., OpenShift OAuth for
  authentication).
- Assess feasibility, effort, and dependency risk per tool (vendor
  coordination, licensing, API availability).
- Produce a prioritized recommendation: which integrations to build first,
  what each would deliver, and what the measurement of "integrates better"
  would be.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A named list of enterprise tools with the account evidence behind each
  entry; no tool enters the list without a feedback source.
- Each named tool has an integration-surface assessment grounded in the
  platform architecture context.
- A prioritized recommendation with rationale, including which items need
  external/vendor coordination and which are achievable with platform changes
  alone.
- The recommendation identifies what the first integration increment will be
  and its acceptance measure.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3: The platform should integrate better with existing enterprise
  tooling. This investigation resolves the unnamed-tools unknown that gates
  all HLR-3 implementation work.

# Dashboard onboarding experience

## Description

Implements the Dashboard-side of the data-scientist onboarding improvements
(what this covers is set by the onboarding scope investigation's decision
record). Where the defined onboarding path runs through the Dashboard console
— project setup, workbench creation flow, and first-run guidance — this epic
delivers the changes that remove the time consumers the baseline identified,
so a new data scientist reaches the defined first-success event in less than a
day.

## Scope

- Implement the Dashboard onboarding changes enumerated in the onboarding
  scope decision record for console-owned steps (e.g., project setup flow,
  workbench spawn flow, defaults that reduce decisions a new user must make).
- Reduce or eliminate the Dashboard-owned friction points identified in the
  baseline time breakdown.
- Keep the flows measurable: the defined onboarding measurement (start event
  to first-success event) can be evaluated end to end through the console.
- Update captions, labels, and references that fall out of these changes (no
  new documentation topics).

## Acceptance Criteria

- All Dashboard-owned steps named in the onboarding decision record are
  implemented as specified there.
- A walkthrough of the defined onboarding path through the console no longer
  includes the Dashboard-owned time consumers identified in the baseline,
  verified against the measurement definition from the decision record.
- Existing project and workbench workflows are preserved; a regression suite
  demonstrates no behavioral change for untouched flows.
- The Dashboard build pipeline is green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2: Onboarding a new data scientist should take less than a day —
  delivers the console portion of the defined onboarding scope.

## Gate

Scoped by the outcome of the onboarding scope investigation; if that outcome
narrows or shifts the onboarding boundary, this epic's scope is rewritten to
match the decision record rather than proceeding on assumptions.

# Notebooks first-workbench onboarding experience

## Description

Implements the workbench (Notebooks) side of the data-scientist onboarding
improvements (what this covers is set by the onboarding scope investigation's
decision record). Where the defined onboarding path involves starting a first
workbench — image selection, spawn time, and first-use defaults reconciled by
the notebook-controller — this epic delivers the changes that remove the time
consumers the baseline identified on that leg.

## Scope

- Implement the workbench-side changes enumerated in the onboarding scope
  decision record (e.g., first-workbench defaults, spawn-path friction
  owned by the notebook-controller, image selection guidance for the first
  workbench). Any console-surface steps of the onboarding path (including
  changes to the Dashboard spawn UI) are apportioned by that decision
  record to the console onboarding work, not pre-assigned here.
- Reduce or eliminate the workbench-owned friction points identified in the
  baseline time breakdown (e.g., wait time to first usable workbench).
- Preserve existing workbench lifecycle behavior for users beyond the
  onboarding path, including the idle culling behavior administered through
  the Dashboard configuration.
- Update captions, labels, and references that fall out of these changes (no
  new documentation topics).

## Acceptance Criteria

- All workbench-side steps named in the onboarding decision record are
  implemented as specified there.
- The workbench leg of the defined onboarding path no longer includes the
